text: The area of the region bounded by the curves $x(1+y^{2})=1$ and $y^{2}=2x$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The curves are $x=\dfrac{1}{1+y^{2}}$ and $x=\dfrac{y^{2}}{2}$.

Intersection: $\dfrac{1}{1+y^{2}}=\dfrac{y^{2}}{2}\Rightarrow y^{4}+y^{2}-2=0\Rightarrow (y^{2}+2)(y^{2}-1)=0\Rightarrow y=\pm 1$, $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$; the points are $\left (\dfrac{1}{2},\pm 1\right )$.


[IMG]

For $-1\leq y\leq 1$ the curve $x=\dfrac{1}{1+y^{2}}$ lies to the right of the parabola (at $y=0$: $1>0$).

$A=\int\limits _{-1}^{1}\left (\frac{1}{1+y^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right )dy=\left [\tan ^{-1}y-\frac{y^{3}}{6}\right ]_{-1}^{1}=\left (\frac{π}{4}+\frac{π}{4}\right )-\left (\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}\right )=\frac{π}{2}-\frac{1}{3}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: Bag $B_{1}$ contains 6 white and 4 blue balls, Bag $B_{2}$ contains 4 white and 6 blue balls, and Bag $B_{3}$ contains 5 white and 5 blue balls. One of the bags is selected at random and a ball is drawn from it. If the ball is white, then the probability that the ball is drawn from Bag $B_{2}$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$E_{1}:$ Bag $B_{1}$ is selected

$\begin{array}{lll} B_{1} & B_{2} & B_{3} \\ 6\mathrm{W}4\mathrm{B} & 4\mathrm{W}6\mathrm{B} & 5\mathrm{W}5\mathrm{B} \end{array}$

$E_{2}:$ bag $B_{2}$ is selected

$E_{3}:$ Bag $B_{3}$ is selected

A : Drawn ball is white

We have to find $P\left (\frac{E_{2}}{A}\right )$

$\begin{array}{l} P\left (\dfrac{E_{2}}{A}\right )=\dfrac{P(E_{2})P\left (\frac{A}{E_{2}}\right )}{P(E_{1})P\left (\frac{A}{E_{1}}\right )+P(E_{2})P\left (\frac{A}{E_{2}}\right )+P(E_{3})P\left (\frac{A}{E_{3}}\right )} \\ =\dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{4}{10}}{\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{6}{10}+\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{4}{10}+\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{5}{10}} \\ =\dfrac{4}{15} \end{array}$

text: Let $\mathrm{f}:\mathrm{R}\to \mathrm{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f(2)=1$. If $\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}f(\mathrm{x})$ for all $\mathrm{x}\in \mathrm{R}$, $\int\limits _{0}^{2}xF^{'}(x)dx=6$ and $\int\limits _{0}^{2}x^{2}F^{''}(x)dx=40$, then $F^{'}(2)+\int\limits _{0}^{2}F(x)dx$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $F(x)=xf(x)$ and $f(2)=1$, so $F(2)=2f(2)=2$.

Integrating by parts,

$\int\limits _{0}^{2}xF^{'}(x)dx=\left [xF(x)\right ]_{0}^{2}-\int\limits _{0}^{2}F(x)dx=2F(2)-\int\limits _{0}^{2}F(x)dx$

So $4-\int\limits _{0}^{2}F(x)dx=6$, which gives $\int\limits _{0}^{2}F(x)dx=-2$.

Again by parts,

$\int\limits _{0}^{2}x^{2}F^{''}(x)dx=\left [x^{2}F^{'}(x)\right ]_{0}^{2}-2\int\limits _{0}^{2}xF^{'}(x)dx=4F^{'}(2)-2\times 6$

So $4F^{'}(2)-12=40$, which gives $F^{'}(2)=13$.

Therefore $F^{'}(2)+\int\limits _{0}^{2}F(x)dx=13-2=11$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: If the midpoint of a chord of the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{9}+\frac{y^{2}}{4}=1$ is $(\sqrt{2},4/3)$, and the length of the chord is $\frac{2\sqrt{α}}{3}$, then $α$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \text{If}\mathrm{m}\left (\sqrt{2},\dfrac{4}{3}\right )\text{than equation of of}\mathrm{AB}\text{is} \\ \begin{array}{l} \mathrm{T}=\mathrm{S}_{1} \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{x}\sqrt{2}}{9}+\dfrac{\mathrm{y}}{4}\left (\dfrac{4}{3}\right )=\dfrac{(\sqrt{2})^{2}}{9}+\dfrac{\left (\frac{4}{3}\right )^{2}}{4} \\ \dfrac{\sqrt{2}\mathrm{x}}{9}+\dfrac{\mathrm{y}}{3}=\dfrac{2}{9}+\dfrac{4}{9} \end{array} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \sqrt{2}x+3y=6\Rightarrow y=\dfrac{6-\sqrt{2}x}{3}\text{put in ellipse} \\ \begin{array}{l} \text{So,}\dfrac{x^{2}}{9}+\dfrac{(6-\sqrt{2}x)^{2}}{9\times 4}=1 \\ 4x^{2}+36+2x^{2}-12\sqrt{2}x=36 \\ 6x^{2}-12\sqrt{2}x=0 \\ 6x(x-2\sqrt{2})=0 \\ x=0&x=2\sqrt{2} \\ \text{So}y=2y=\dfrac{2}{3} \\ \text{Length of chord}=\sqrt{(2\sqrt{2}-0)^{2}+\left (\dfrac{2}{3}-2\right )^{2}} \\ =\sqrt{8+\dfrac{16}{9}} \\ =\sqrt{\dfrac{88}{9}}=\dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{22}\text{so}α=22 \end{array} \end{array}$

text: Two equal sides of an isosceles triangle are along $-x+2y=4$ and $x+y=4$. If $m$ is the slope of its third side, then the sum, of all possible distinct values of $m$, is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
The lines $-x+2y=4$ and $x+y=4$ have slopes $m_{1}=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $m_{2}=-1$. They carry the two equal sides, so the third side (the base, slope $m$) makes equal angles $θ$ with both of them.


[IMG]

$\left |\dfrac{m-\frac{1}{2}}{1+\frac{m}{2}}\right |=\left |\dfrac{m+1}{1-m}\right |\Rightarrow \dfrac{2m-1}{m+2}=\pm \dfrac{m+1}{1-m}$

With the $+$ sign: $(2m-1)(1-m)=(m+1)(m+2)\Rightarrow -2m^{2}+3m-1=m^{2}+3m+2\Rightarrow m^{2}=-1$, which has no real root.

With the $-$ sign: $(2m-1)(m-1)=(m+1)(m+2)\Rightarrow 2m^{2}-3m+1=m^{2}+3m+2\Rightarrow m^{2}-6m-1=0$, so $m=3\pm \sqrt{10}$.

These two slopes are perpendicular to the two angle bisectors of the given lines, and each gives an isosceles triangle, so the sum of all possible values of $m$ is $6$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: Let $f:𝐑-\{0\}\to (-\infty ,1)$ be a polynomial of degree 2 , satisfying $f(x)f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=f(x)+f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )$. If $f(\mathrm{K})=-2\mathrm{K}$, then the sum of squares of all possible values of K is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given relation $f(x)f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=f(x)+f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )$ is equivalent to $(f(x)-1)\left (f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )-1\right )=1$.

Let $g(x)=f(x)-1=ax^{2}+bx+d$ with $a\neq 0$. Then $g(x)g\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=1$, and multiplying by $x^{2}$:

$(ax^{2}+bx+d)(dx^{2}+bx+a)=x^{2}\text{for all}x\neq 0$

The coefficient of $x^{4}$ gives $ad=0$, so $d=0$. Then $(ax^{2}+bx)(bx+a)=x^{2}$, i.e. $abx^{3}+(a^{2}+b^{2})x^{2}+abx=x^{2}$, so $ab=0$ and $a^{2}+b^{2}=1$, giving $b=0$, $a=\pm 1$.

Thus $f(x)=1\pm x^{2}$. Since $f(x)<1$ for every $x\neq 0$, $f(x)=1-x^{2}$.

Now $f(K)=-2K$ gives $1-K^{2}=-2K$, i.e. $K^{2}-2K-1=0$, whose roots $K=1\pm \sqrt{2}$ are both non-zero.

$K_{1}^{2}+K_{2}^{2}=(K_{1}+K_{2})^{2}-2K_{1}K_{2}=4-2(-1)=6$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: If A and B are the points of intersection of the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-8x=0$ and the hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{9}-\frac{y^{2}}{4}=1$ and a point P moves on the line $2x-3y+4=0$, then the centroid of $\Delta PAB$ lies on the line :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
From the circle, $y^{2}=8x-x^{2}$; the hyperbola is $4x^{2}-9y^{2}=36$. Substituting,

$4x^{2}-9\left (8x-x^{2}\right )=36\Rightarrow 13x^{2}-72x-36=0\Rightarrow (13x+6)(x-6)=0$

For $x=-\dfrac{6}{13}$, $y^{2}=8x-x^{2}<0$, so it is rejected. For $x=6$, $y^{2}=48-36=12$, so $A\left (6,2\sqrt{3}\right )$ and $B\left (6,-2\sqrt{3}\right )$.

A point on $2x-3y+4=0$ is $P\left (α,\dfrac{2α+4}{3}\right )$. The centroid $(h,k)$ of $△PAB$ is

$h=\dfrac{6+6+α}{3}\Rightarrow α=3h-12,k=\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{3}+\frac{2α+4}{3}}{3}\Rightarrow 9k=2α+4$

Eliminating $α$: $9k=2(3h-12)+4=6h-20$, so the centroid lies on $6x-9y=20$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: If $f(x)=\int \frac{1}{x^{1/4}\left (1+x^{1/4}\right )}\mathrm{d}x,f(0)=-6$, then $f(1)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Substitution: Start by substituting $x=t^{4}$ which implies $dx=4t^{3}dt$.

Integral Transformation:

$\int \frac{1}{x^{1/4}(1+x^{1/4})}dx\Rightarrow \int \frac{4t^{3}dt}{t(1+t)}=\int \frac{4t^{2}}{1+t}dt$

Rewriting the Integral: The expression $\frac{4t^{2}}{1+t}$ can be decomposed as:

$\frac{4t^{2}}{1+t}=4\left (\frac{t^{2}-1+1}{1+t}\right )=4\left ((t-1)+\frac{1}{t+1}\right )$

Separate and Integrate:

$4\int (t-1)dt+4\int \frac{1}{t+1}dt$

Solving the Integrals:

The integral of $t-1$ is $\frac{(t-1)^{2}}{2}$.

The integral of $\frac{1}{t+1}$ is $\ln (t+1)$.

Therefore:

$f(x)=4\left \{\frac{(t-1)^{2}}{2}+\ln (t+1)\right \}+C$

Substitute $t=x^{1/4}$: Replace $t$ back with $x^{1/4}$:

$f(x)=2(x^{1/4}-1)^{2}+4\ln (1+x^{1/4})+C$

Using the Condition $f(0)=-6$:

$f(0)=2(0-1)^{2}+4\ln (1+0)+C=2\times 1-0+C=-6$

Solving gives $C=-8$.

Find $f(1)$:

$f(1)=2(1^{1/4}-1)^{2}+4\ln (1+1^{1/4})-8$

Simplifies to:

$f(1)=0+4\ln 2-8=4(\ln 2-2)$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$ and $\mathrm{P}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos θ & -\sin θ \\ \sin θ & \cos θ \end{array}\right ],θ>0$. If $\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{PAP}{}^{⊤},\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{P}^{⊤}\mathrm{B}^{10}\mathrm{P}$ and the sum of the diagonal elements of $C$ is $\frac{m}{n}$, where $\gcd (m,n)=1$, then $m+n$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $P^{\mathrm{T}}P=PP^{\mathrm{T}}=I$, $B^{2}=PAP^{\mathrm{T}}PAP^{\mathrm{T}}=PA^{2}P^{\mathrm{T}}$, and in the same way $B^{10}=PA^{10}P^{\mathrm{T}}$.

Hence $C=P^{\mathrm{T}}B^{10}P=(P^{\mathrm{T}}P)A^{10}(P^{\mathrm{T}}P)=A^{10}$.

$A$ is upper triangular with diagonal entries $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $1$. A product of upper triangular matrices is upper triangular, with diagonal entries equal to the products of the corresponding diagonal entries, so

$C=A^{10}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \left (\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{10} & \ast  \\ 0 & 1^{10} \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \dfrac{1}{32} & \ast  \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ].$

Sum of the diagonal elements of $C$ $=\dfrac{1}{32}+1=\dfrac{33}{32}$, so $m=33$, $n=32$ with $\gcd (33,32)=1$, and $m+n=65$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

solution.body:
From $g(x^{3})=x^{6}+x^{7}$, replacing $x$ by $x^{1/3}$ gives $g(x)=x^{2}+x^{7/3}$ for $x>0$.

Since $g(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}tf(t)dt$ with $f$ continuous, $g^{'}(x)=xf(x)$. Also $g^{'}(x)=2x+\dfrac{7}{3}x^{4/3}$, so

$f(x)=2+\dfrac{7}{3}x^{1/3}\Rightarrow f(r^{3})=2+\dfrac{7r}{3}$

Therefore

$\sum\limits _{r=1}^{15}f(r^{3})=2\times 15+\dfrac{7}{3}\cdot \dfrac{15\times 16}{2}=30+280=310$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: For positive integers $n$, if $4a_{n}=\left (n^{2}+5n+6\right )$ and $S_{n}=\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\left (\frac{1}{a_{k}}\right )$, then the value of $507S_{2025}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}} & =\dfrac{\mathrm{n}^{2}+5\mathrm{n}+6}{4} \\ \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}} & =\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}}=\sum\limits _{\mathrm{k}=1}^{\mathrm{n}}\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{k}}}=\sum\limits _{1}^{\mathrm{n}}\dfrac{4}{\mathrm{k}^{2}+5\mathrm{k}+6} \\ =4\sum\limits _{\mathrm{k}=1}^{\mathrm{n}}\dfrac{1}{(\mathrm{k}+2)(\mathrm{k}+3)} \\ =4\sum\limits _{\mathrm{k}=1}^{\mathrm{n}}\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{k}+2}-\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{k}+3} \\ =4\left (\dfrac{1}{3}-\dfrac{1}{4}\right )+4\left (\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{5}\right )+\ldots \ldots .. \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} 4\left (\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}+2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}+3}\right ) \\ =4\left (\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}+3}\right ) \\ =\frac{4\mathrm{n}}{3(\mathrm{n}+3)} \\ {}^{507}\mathrm{S}_{2025}=\frac{(507)(4)(2025)}{3(2028)} \\ =675 \end{array}$

text: Let $f(x)=\lim _{n\to \infty }\sum\limits _{r=0}^{n}\left (\frac{\tan \left (x/2^{r+1}\right )+\tan ^{3}\left (x/2^{r+1}\right )}{1-\tan ^{2}(x/2^{r+1})}\right )$. Then $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{e^{x}-e^{f(x)}}{(x-f(x))}$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $θ=\dfrac{x}{2^{r+1}}$ and $t=\tan θ$. Then

$\tan 2θ-\tan θ=\frac{2t}{1-t^{2}}-t=\frac{t+t^{3}}{1-t^{2}},$

so the $r$-th term equals $\tan \dfrac{x}{2^{r}}-\tan \dfrac{x}{2^{r+1}}$.

The sum telescopes:

$\sum\limits _{r=0}^{n}\left (\tan \frac{x}{2^{r}}-\tan \frac{x}{2^{r+1}}\right )=\tan x-\tan \frac{x}{2^{n+1}}.$

As $n\to \infty$, $\tan \dfrac{x}{2^{n+1}}\to 0$, so $f(x)=\tan x$.

Then

$\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{e^{x}-e^{\tan x}}{x-\tan x}=\lim _{x\to 0}e^{\tan x}\cdot \frac{e^{x-\tan x}-1}{x-\tan x}.$

As $x\to 0$, $e^{\tan x}\to 1$, and $u=x-\tan x\to 0$ with $u\neq 0$ for $x\neq 0$, so $\dfrac{e^{u}-1}{u}\to 1$. The limit is $1\times 1=1$.

Hence, the answer is 1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
If $y=y(x)$ is the solution of the differential equation,
$\sqrt{4-x^{2}}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\left (\left (\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{x}{2}\right )\right )^{2}-y\right )\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{x}{2}\right ),-2\leq x\leq 2,y(2)=\frac{π^{2}-8}{4}$, then $y^{2}(0)$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Put $θ=\sin ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{x}{2}\right )$, so $dθ=\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{4-x^{2}}}$ and the equation becomes

$\dfrac{dy}{dθ}=(θ^{2}-y)θ\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dθ}+θy=θ^{3}.$

The integrating factor is $e^{\int θdθ}=e^{θ^{2}/2}$, so

$y~e^{θ^{2}/2}=\int θ^{3}e^{θ^{2}/2}dθ.$

With $u=\dfrac{θ^{2}}{2}$, $du=θdθ$: $\int 2ue^{u}du=2(u-1)e^{u}=(θ^{2}-2)e^{θ^{2}/2}$. Hence

$y=θ^{2}-2+ce^{-θ^{2}/2}.$

At $x=2$, $θ=\dfrac{π}{2}$: $\dfrac{π^{2}}{4}-2+ce^{-π^{2}/8}=\dfrac{π^{2}-8}{4}$, so $c=0$ and $y=\left (\sin ^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}\right )^{2}-2$.

At $x=0$, $θ=0$, so $y(0)=-2$ and $y^{2}(0)=4$.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: The interior angles of a polygon with n sides, are in an A.P. with common difference 6°. If the largest interior angle of the polygon is 219°, then n is equal to $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\mathrm{n}}{2}(2\mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{n}-1)6)=(\mathrm{n}-2)\cdot 180^{\circ } \\ \mathrm{an}+3\mathrm{n}^{2}-3\mathrm{n}=(\mathrm{n}-2)\cdot 180^{\circ }\text{.... (1)} \end{array}$

Now according to question

$\begin{array}{l} a+(n-1)6^{\circ }=219^{\circ } \\ \Rightarrow a=225^{\circ }-6n^{\circ }\text{.... (2)} \end{array}$

Putting value of a from equation (2) in (1)

We get

$\begin{array}{l} \left (225\mathrm{n}-6\mathrm{n}^{2}\right )+3\mathrm{n}^{2}-3\mathrm{n}=180\mathrm{n}-360 \\ \Rightarrow 3\mathrm{n}^{2}-42\mathrm{n}-360=0 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}^{2}-14\mathrm{n}-120=0 \\ \mathrm{n}=20,-6\text{(rejected)} \end{array}$
